purpose: Evaluate context-appropriate color storytelling and relational harmony, separately from liking and numerical correctness.

controls: same fixed renderer, composition, text and geometry
randomized anonymous labels and presentation order
design.preregistration: Before generation, freeze brief set, arm snapshots, renderer, rubric anchors, revision budget, reviewer instructions and analysis plan. These development briefs are visible to the author and are NOT held out. Use separately authored unseen briefs for claims of transfer.
design.renderRequirement: Independent fresh reviewer must actually inspect live rendered pixels for each evaluated revision. If blocked, mark not run; no code-only judgement.

reviewStages: Hide arm identity, brief and author rationale. Ask for perceived story/qualities and first noticed element in free text.
Reveal brief, but not rationale. Rate brief fit, relational harmony, attention hierarchy and appropriate distinctiveness using anchored 1–5 scales, concrete observations and confidence.
Read rationale only after visual ratings are fixed; assess correspondence to visible choices separately.
Record preference last, with reason if offered. Do not infer a reason for an unexplained vote.

briefFit.1: Contradicts intended meaning or strongly evokes the explicitly avoided reading.
briefFit.3: Broadly suitable but generic or mixed cues.
briefFit.5: Distinctive and consistent support for the stated context and story.

relationalHarmony.1: Unintended clashes or disconnected dominant/support/focal relationships.
relationalHarmony.3: Mostly coherent, with a visible competing or weak relationship.
relationalHarmony.5: Colors belong together at their actual areas and adjacency; deliberate tension is integrated.

attentionHierarchy.1: Wrong element dominates or required focal/action region is lost.
attentionHierarchy.3: Intended order can be found but competition remains.
attentionHierarchy.5: Declared attention order reads clearly without unnecessary competition.

appropriateDistinctiveness.1: Generic or novelty conflicts with the brief.
appropriateDistinctiveness.5: Recognizable character serves this brief without sacrificing meaning or use.

hardGates: all specified text/background contrasts verified from actual rendered usage
color is not the sole required semantic cue
required roles, source fidelity and gamut constraints checked when applicable
outcomes: blind human story attribution and coding against a frozen intent codebook
per-dimension human rating distributions and paired differences
observed task correctness when the brief has a functional task
measurement.analysis: Report per brief and across briefs, ties, disagreement, sample sizes and uncertainty. Do not collapse everything into an objective beauty percentage. If only model critics participated, label results model-critic development feedback, not human validation.
measurement.audience: Recruit relevant audience only with authorization; no outreach or participant data collection is authorized by this file. Multiple independent raters and briefs are needed before a general performance claim.

briefs.context: Reading app returning after a stressful day
Service dashboard with a real urgent issue
Independent editorial cover challenging an established convention

limitations: No generated candidates or visual evaluation yet.
Guidance and protocol-integrity tests do not demonstrate improved color judgement.
Subjective harmony has no universal numerical ground truth.
Story recognition can be affected by copy and imagery; keep them fixed for within-brief comparisons and report the limitation.
